title: Monday Teacher Plan
note: Short week: Mon–Thu, Thursday is turn-in day (Fri Nov 20 minimum day). Monday = expectations Wayground + grade check. 7th votes on bridges for DONUTS (air Tuesday).

4th Period.topic: Electrical engineering, Circuits 1: Blink an LED (TinkerCAD Circuits)
4th Period.goal: By the end of class, my TinkerCAD circuit blinks an LED, and I can say what the resistor is for.
4th Period.exitTicket: What does the resistor protect, and what happens without it?
prep: Circuits 1: Blink assignment on Google Classroom (no handout today)
Exit ticket question posted with sentence frames
Your own TinkerCAD Circuits blink circuit open to model

segments.title: Wayground: classroom expectations
segments.do: Students take the classroom expectations Wayground (Monday's standing quiz).
segments.why: Predictable Monday start; resets norms after the weekend (Maslow: safety).
tips: Watch live results for the most-missed expectation.

segments.title: Grade check: Infinite Campus + form
segments.do: Students open Infinite Campus, find their overall grade, and fill out the Weekly Grade Check-In (2026-2027) form.
segments.why: Weekly self-monitoring; no surprises at progress reports.
tips: Keep grades private: no screens shown to neighbors.
Below 70%: point to the regrade form and Tuesday tutoring. Exit tickets can't be redone; missing work is accepted late for full credit.

segments.title: This week (4 days) and the points
segments.do: Electrical engineering starts today. Walk the week: Mon blink, Tue button, Wed dial, Thu servo + turn in once. Read the goal aloud: By the end of class, my TinkerCAD circuit blinks an LED, and I can say what the resistor is for.
segments.why: A new unit needs a clear arc; students know Thursday's product before they start.
tips: Say it plainly: we're done with Copilot and games; this is circuits now.

segments.title: I do: breadboard, Arduino, LED, resistor
segments.do: Build the blink circuit live in TinkerCAD Circuits: how breadboard rows connect, LED legs (long = +), the 220 Ω resistor in series, pin 13, then the blink code.
segments.why: Worked example first; every part is named before students touch it.
tips: Ask: what happens without the resistor? (Too much current; the LED burns out.)
Leave your finished circuit on the projector.

segments.title: You do: build and blink your LED
segments.do: Students build the same circuit in their own TinkerCAD Circuits, start the simulation, and change the delay so it blinks faster or slower.
segments.why: Hands-on build with a visible success signal.
tips: Most common bug: LED backwards or resistor in the wrong row.
Fast finishers: blink two LEDs in turn.

segments.title: Share your circuit link
segments.do: Students copy their TinkerCAD share link into the Classroom assignment.
segments.why: Thursday's turn-in is the week's links; collecting them daily prevents a scramble.

segments.title: Exit Ticket: what does the resistor protect?
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom with a sentence frame.
segments.why: Checks the one idea that matters most today.

watchFor: LED in backwards (long leg goes toward the pin)
Resistor in the same row as nothing (breadboard rows)
Students who haven't signed in to TinkerCAD with their school account

6th Period.topic: Cam and Follower, Day 1: how a cam works + DONUTS bridge vote
6th Period.goal: By the end of class, I can explain how a cam turns spinning motion into up-and-down motion.
6th Period.exitTicket: What happens to the follower when the cam spins?
prep: Exit ticket posted on the Cam and Follower assignment with both frames
Bridge photos/videos from Friday's break test ready to show for the vote
Vote method ready (hand vote or quick form): top 3, not your own group

segments.title: Wayground: classroom expectations
segments.do: Students take the classroom expectations Wayground (Monday's standing quiz).
segments.why: Predictable Monday start; resets norms after the weekend (Maslow: safety).
tips: Watch live results for the most-missed expectation.

segments.title: Review answers + today's goal
segments.do: Re-teach the most-missed expectation, then read the goal aloud: By the end of class, I can explain how a cam turns spinning motion into up-and-down motion.
segments.why: Students know the target before any directions.
tips: Frame it positively: name the expectation, then what it looks like in our room.
Point to the goal again halfway through and at the exit ticket.

segments.do: Students open Infinite Campus, find their overall grade, and fill out the Weekly Grade Check-In (2026-2027) form.
segments.why: Weekly self-monitoring; no surprises at progress reports.
tips: Keep grades private: no screens shown to neighbors.
Below 70%: point to the regrade form and Tuesday tutoring. Exit tickets can't be redone; missing work is accepted late for full credit.

segments.title: DONUTS vote: top 3 bridges
segments.do: Show each group's bridge and break result, then students vote for their top 3 (not their own group).
segments.why: Peer recognition is the motivator (PBL public product); bridges had real design freedom.
tips: Criteria on the handout: how much it held, how clean the build, how cool the break.
Winners air Tuesday on DONUTS: tell them.

segments.title: This week (4 days) and the points
segments.do: Walk the week: Mon how a cam works, Tue model the cam in TinkerCAD, Wed add the follower, Thu label, screenshot, turn in once. Points: 70 floor + 10/10/10.
segments.why: Points and the single turn-in shown up front lower anxiety (Maslow).
tips: Say it plainly: today they write only the exit ticket.
No class Friday (minimum day). Thursday is turn-in day; due Sunday 11:59 PM.

segments.title: Mini-lesson: cams and followers
segments.do: Use the LOW/HIGH diagram. Key words: CAM (off-center wheel), FOLLOWER (rides on top), AXLE (stays put). Read THE KEY RULE together. Quick examples: engine valves, sewing machine needle, bobbing toy heads.
segments.why: Concrete visual before vocabulary (ELD: pre-teach words with pictures).
tips: Act it out: fist = cam on a pencil axle, other hand flat on top = follower.
10-2: after the lesson, 2-minute turn-and-talk: 'Where is the big side when the follower is high?'

segments.title: We do: sketch a cam and follower
segments.do: Box 1: axle dot near the bottom, follower on top. Box 2: same cam half a turn later (axle near the top), follower drawn, arrow up or down.
segments.why: Students produce the model themselves (Bloom: Understand).
tips: Answer key: Box 1 follower is HIGH (big side up); Box 2 follower is LOW (big side down), arrow ↓.
Freehand circles are fine: no rulers needed.

segments.title: Exit Ticket: what does a cam do?
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom with a frame.
segments.why: One turn-in; checks today's goal.
tips: Answer key: the follower moves up and down because the axle is off-center; a cam turns spinning (rotary) motion into up-and-down motion.
Recap the goal before they write.

watchFor: Students who put the axle in the center (nothing moves: use it as a teachable 'why off-center' moment Tuesday)
Vote turning into a popularity contest: re-read the criteria

7th Period.topic: Tensegrity, Day 1: feel tension with a stick and string
7th Period.goal: By the end of class, I can explain how tension in string holds sticks up in a tensegrity.
7th Period.exitTicket: What is tension, and what happened to the stick when the string went loose?
prep: Exit ticket posted on the Tensegrity assignment with both frames
Per pair: 1 popsicle stick, string, scissors; folded-paper measuring sticks out
A string + stick of your own to demo

segments.title: Wayground: classroom expectations
segments.do: Students take the classroom expectations Wayground (Monday's standing quiz).
segments.why: Predictable Monday start; resets norms after the weekend (Maslow: safety).
tips: Watch live results for the most-missed expectation.

segments.title: This week (4 days) and the points
segments.do: Walk the week: Mon tension, Tue tie a 3-stick frame in pairs, Wed tighten until it stands, Thu push test, photo, turn in once. Points: 70 floor + 10/10/10.
segments.why: Points and the single turn-in shown up front lower anxiety (Maslow).
tips: Pitch the challenge: a tensegrity that stands on its own looks impossible, and it's on them to make it.
No class Friday (minimum day). Thursday is turn-in day; due Sunday 11:59 PM.

segments.title: Mini-lesson: push and pull
segments.do: Use the push/pull diagram: strings can't push (floppy), pulled strings = TENSION, pushed sticks = COMPRESSION. Show the 3-stick tensegrity picture: no stick touches another.
segments.why: Vocabulary tied to a picture and a physical action (ELD; Bloom: Understand).
tips: Demo with your own string: push it (floppy), pull it (tight).
Real-world hook: bike wheel spokes are all in tension.

segments.title: Roles by birthday
segments.do: Pairs line up by birthday: younger = Holder, older = Tester. One group of 3 if odd: oldest = Checker.
segments.why: Complex Instruction: roles with real jobs; students never choose.
tips: Remind them to swap roles before test 5.

segments.title: We do: feel tension with a stick and string
segments.do: Pairs run tests 1–6: cut string 2 sticks long, push test, pull test, stick test, predict, hold-up test (tight vs loose).
segments.why: Hands-on before explaining (ADHD-friendly movement; Bloom: Apply). Prediction before the test adds rigor for a class that wants challenge.
tips: Answer key: push → floppy; pull → tight, pushes back on a finger (tension); stick pushes back (compression); loose string → the stick drops / hangs, tight → stays up.
Knots slipping: wrap twice around the stick, then tie.
Assign competence: praise a pair whose prediction came with a reason.
Revisit the goal halfway through.

segments.title: Exit Ticket: what is tension?
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom with a frame.
segments.why: One turn-in, directly answerable from the tests they ran.
tips: Answer key: tension is a pull; when the string went loose, the stick dropped/sagged.
Extra time: clean up string scraps and sticks, and start Future Engineer.

watchFor: Pushing too hard on the stick in the stick test (gentle!)

accommodations: Goal read after the Wayground and revisited mid-lesson, numbered steps, worked example first, checklists, sentence frames on every exit ticket, frequent check-ins, positive reinforcement.
Key words tied to diagrams (COLLECTION/ITEM/ITERATOR; CAM/FOLLOWER/AXLE; TENSION/COMPRESSION), turn-and-talk before writing, two frames per exit ticket, Immersive Reader.
Lexend Deca handouts, steps read aloud, speech-to-text OK, spelling not graded; 8th: Ctrl + F instead of scanning code by eye.
Short timed chunks with a visual timer, hands-on roles (Holder/Tester), acting out the cam with hands, preferential seating near the demo, discreet redirection, break pass.

Extended time, dictated exit tickets, intentional partners, grades not penalized for behavior. Floors: 8th labels 3 loops; 7th draws Box 1 only and answers with one frame; 6th does pull test + hold-up test only.
Future Engineer (OPTIONAL): 1 KB point. 8th busiest loop / spark iterator / portfolio; 7th snail cam / quarter turns / real cam; 6th one vs two strings / spot tension / best knot.
frameworks: Each grade starts a 4-day build toward one Thursday product: cleaned-up loops in a live game, a TinkerCAD cam, a standing tensegrity. 7th's bridge vote puts last week's product on DONUTS.
Birthday-order roles in 6th; 8th checks Copilot rather than trusting it; publicly assign competence (caught a missed loop, a reasoned prediction).
Expectations Wayground, grade check, points and one turn-in shown up front, 'you are not behind'.
Monday is Remember/Understand (6th: Understand/Apply); the week climbs to Apply/Create Tue–Wed and Evaluate Thursday.
